from.place: Proof paragraph 2 of prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint: derived coefficient adjunction, via the stable enhancement and finite pushout grid of lem-coef-suspension-square-comparison; local cone filling in the mapping-space universal property of pointwise Kan diagrams. Proposition 7.3.4.7, implication (2) to (1), with Proposition 7.3.4.3 (02ZP) identifying the fiber cones. No separate quasicategory assertion is needed here. title: Relative join extension over one simplex with its full boundary fixed
statement: Use simplicial sets, quasicategories and standard simplices of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], relative joins of [def-coef-infinity-relative-join], relative colimit diagrams of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone], and cocartesian fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Fix $n\geq1$, put $S=\Delta^n$, and let $\partial S$ be the union of its proper faces. Let $u:X\to S$ be a cocartesian fibration of quasicategories. Put $Y=X\star_S S$, with projection $\pi:Y\to S$ given by the $S$ coordinate in its relative-join pullback, and let $M=i_X(X)\cup\pi^{-1}(\partial S)\subseteq Y$. Let $p:D\to B$ be an isofibration of quasicategories, meaning an inner fibration such that every equivalence edge $e:p(d)\to b_0$ lifts to an equivalence edge $\widetilde e:d\to\widetilde b_0$ with $p(\widetilde e)=e$. Suppose $a:M\to D$ and $b:Y\to B$ are simplicial maps satisfying $pa=b|_M$ exactly. Write $X_0=X\times_S\{0\}$ and $j_0:X_0^{\triangleright}\to Y$ for its fiber-cone inclusion. Since $n\geq1$, this inclusion lands in $M$. Assume $aj_0:X_0^{\triangleright}\to D$ is a $p$-colimit diagram. Then there exists a simplicial map $\widetilde a:Y\to D$ satisfying $\widetilde a|_M=a$ and $p\widetilde a=b$ exactly. No colimit condition is imposed on the other vertex cones, and no preservation of colimits by fiber transport is assumed. All objects are small in a fixed sufficiently large universe.

source.place: Lemma 7.3.4.5 with C = Delta^n and C_0 = boundary Delta^n, n >= 1. A simplex not in the boundary is surjective on the vertices of [n], hence starts at 0, so condition (*) only requires the displayed initial-vertex cone. Read online; not archived. This is a Kerodon identifier, not a Stacks tag.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-relative-join-cocartesian-projection] to $u:X\to S$. Thus $Y$ is a quasicategory, $\pi:Y\to S$ is cocartesian, and $i_X$ preserves cocartesian edges. The formulas of [def-coef-infinity-relative-join] identify $Y_s$ with $X_s^{\triangleright}$, including the map $j_s$: over a constant simplex at $s$, the pullback condition says exactly that the initial join block belongs to $X_s$ and the final block is the unique simplex of a point. They also identify $T\times_S Y$ with $(T\times_S X)\star_T T$ for every $T\to S$: retain the same join blocks, interval parameter and base simplex, now labeled by the simplex of $T$. When $T$ is a quasicategory, $T\times_S X$ is a quasicategory: fill an inner horn in $T$, then lift its chosen filler along $u$. The pulled-back projection is cocartesian directly from its horn and edge-lift definitions: pair each chosen lift or filler in $X$ with the prescribed simplex in $T$. Consequently, applying the cited join lemma over $T=\Delta^1$ shows that the inclusion on each edge pullback preserves all cocartesian edges. The inclusion $i_X$ is degreewise injective by its pure-block formula.

source.place: Opening construction of the join projection; fiber and edge-pullback identifications. Agent expansion using the cited statements; online source, archival copy wanted.

proof.text: For $Z=X,Y$ and $E=D,B$, define $H_Z(E)_m$ to consist of pairs $(\sigma,h)$ with $\sigma:\Delta^m\to S$ and $h:\Delta^m\times_S Z\to E$, with operators given by restriction. Its projection is a cartesian fibration, and $H_Z(E)$ is a quasicategory, by the opposite dual of [lem-cbc-enhanced-relative-exponential]. Explicitly reverse each ordinal: an operator $\alpha:[k]\to[m]$ becomes $j\mapsto m-\alpha(k-j)$. This reverses the two outer horns and their distinguished edges, so $Z^{\mathrm{op}}\to S^{\mathrm{op}}$ is cartesian. Apply that node with target $E^{\mathrm{op}}$ and reverse back; degreewise its relative Hom is exactly $H_Z(E)$. Its edge criterion becomes: an edge is cartesian precisely when its associated map $\Delta^1\times_S Z\to E$ sends cocartesian edges to equivalences. Postcomposition by $p$ preserves these edges since a simplicial map preserves the inverse-triangle witnesses of equivalences. Restriction along $i_X$ also preserves them, by the edge-pullback preservation proved in Step 1. The strict fiber at $s$ is $\operatorname{Fun}(Z_s,E)$ by the displayed degreewise formula. Finally, maps $K\to H_Z(E)$ over $S$ are exactly maps $K\times_S Z\to E$: the local maps on the simplices of $K$ glue degreewise by the restriction identities. This last description applies to arbitrary simplicial $K$, not just quasicategories.

source.place: Equation (7.22), relative functor categories and their cartesian-edge criterion; Corollary 5.3.6.9 (0472). Agent expansion using the cited statements; online source, archival copy wanted.

proof.text: First combine clause (1) of [lem-coef-joyal-quasicategory-characterizations] with [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]: between quasicategories, the inner-fibration and source-prescribed equivalence-lifting condition is equivalent to being a Joyal fibration, hence to exact lifting against every degreewise injective categorical equivalence. We use this criterion in both directions below. Postcomposition $H_X(D)\to H_X(B)$ is an isofibration. Indeed fix any degreewise injective categorical equivalence $K\hookrightarrow L$ and any lifting square for this map. Its common projection gives $L\to S$. For $Z=X,Y$ write $K_Z=K\times_S Z$ and $L_Z=L\times_S Z$. By [lem-coef-cocartesian-categorical-base-change], $K_Z\hookrightarrow L_Z$ is a categorical equivalence; it is degreewise injective. The adjunction of Step 2 turns the postcomposition square into $K_X\to D$, $L_X\to B$ against $p$. Apply this criterion to $p$ and this inclusion, then curry the exact lift. The same criterion applied between the quasicategories $H_X(D),H_X(B)$ proves the assertion. Restriction $H_Y(B)\to H_X(B)$ is an isofibration as well: the corresponding extension problem into $B$ has domain $W=K_Y\amalg_{K_X}L_X\subseteq L_Y$. The map $K_Y\to W$ is a pushout of the trivial cofibration $K_X\to L_X$ in [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure], hence is a trivial cofibration: push out the left lifting property in its weak factorization system. Since $K_Y\to L_Y$ is a categorical equivalence, two-out-of-three makes $W\to L_Y$ a categorical equivalence; it is a monomorphism because both pieces are subsets of $L_Y$ with intersection $K_X$. The quasicategory $B$ is fibrant in that model structure, so the lifting axiom extends every map $W\to B$. Currying and the categorical-lifting criterion prove the restriction assertion. No small-index colimit theorem is used: this pushout is the degreewise union just described.

source.place: Proof that the maps on relative functor categories are isofibrations; categorical equivalence of the pushout inclusion. Agent expansion using the cited statements; online source, archival copy wanted.

proof.text: Put $Q=H_X(D)\times_{H_X(B)}H_Y(B)$, with its common projection to $S$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-cartesian-fibration-pullback] with $E_0=H_Y(B)$, $E_1=H_X(D)$ and $H=H_X(B)$, identifying its pullback with $Q$ by the explicit simplicial swap $(h_B,h_D)\mapsto(h_D,h_B)$. Step 2 gives the cartesian fibrations, the inner fibration $H\to S$ and preservation of cartesian edges by both comparison maps; Step 3 gives the required isofibration $F_1$, namely postcomposition. Thus $Q$ is a quasicategory, $Q\to S$ is cartesian, and its cartesian edges are precisely pairs of cartesian edges. Define $R:H_Y(D)\to Q$ by $R(h)=(h|_X,ph)$. It preserves cartesian edges by Step 2 and this componentwise criterion. It is an isofibration: a lifting square against $K\hookrightarrow L$ as in Step 3 transposes into the square against $p$ with top domain $W=K_Y\amalg_{K_X}L_X$ and bottom domain $L_Y$. Step 3 already proved that $W\to L_Y$ is a monomorphic categorical equivalence; the criterion of Step 3 for $p$ supplies an exact lift on $L_Y$. Curry it and apply that criterion once more, now between the established quasicategories $H_Y(D)$ and $Q$. In particular $R$ is an inner fibration.

source.place: The pullback projection T-prime of equation (7.22) and the proof that V is an isofibration. Agent expansion using the cited statements; online source, archival copy wanted.

proof.text: Let $f=a|_{i_X(X)}$, identified with a map $X\to D$. The given $b:Y\to B$ and $pf=b|_X$ define a section $\beta:S\to Q$: on a simplex $\sigma$, its components are $f\operatorname{pr}_X$ and $b\operatorname{pr}_Y$. Likewise $a$ on $\pi^{-1}(\partial S)$ defines $\alpha:\partial S\to H_Y(D)$ by $\alpha(\sigma)=(\sigma,a\operatorname{pr}_Y)$. Its restriction component is $f\operatorname{pr}_X$, and its postcomposition component is $b\operatorname{pr}_Y$, because $pa=b|_M$. Thus $R\alpha=\beta|_{\partial S}$ exactly. All these assignments commute with simplicial operators by restriction. Since $n\geq1$, vertex zero is in $\partial S$, so $\alpha(0)$ is the originally specified cone $c=aj_0$, including all its simplices.

source.place: Rewriting equation (7.21) by the relative-Hom adjunction, without replacing any boundary map. Agent expansion using the cited statements; online source, archival copy wanted.

proof.text: Take the strict fiber of $R$ at zero. Step 1 identifies $Y_0=X_0^{\triangleright}$ with the actual inclusion $j_0$, and Step 2 identifies this fiber functor with the corner map $\operatorname{Fun}(X_0^{\triangleright},D)\to\operatorname{Fun}(X_0,D)\times_{\operatorname{Fun}(X_0,B)}\operatorname{Fun}(X_0^{\triangleright},B)$. The hypothesis says that $c=\alpha(0)$ is a $p$-colimit diagram, in precisely the relative sense used by [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-initial-corner]. Apply its colimit clause with $K=X_0$ and the given isofibration $p$. It says that $c$ is initial relative to this entire corner map. By the definition of relative initiality in [lem-coef-infinity-relative-initial-boundary], for every $t\in H_Y(D)_0$ this gives the weak homotopy equivalence $\operatorname{Map}_{H_Y(D)_0}(c,t)\to\operatorname{Map}_{Q_0}(R_0c,R_0t)$. In particular no base diagram of $t$ is required to be fixed.

source.place: Final paragraph: relative colimit implies relative initiality for the fiber corner, Proposition 7.1.6.13. Agent expansion using the cited statements; online source, archival copy wanted.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-cartesian-initial-boundary-lift] to the cartesian fibrations $H_Y(D)\to S$ and $Q\to S$, the inner fibration $R$, and the square $(\alpha,\beta)$. Preservation of cartesian edges was checked in Step 4, the outgoing mapping-space equivalences in the strict zero fiber are Step 6, and the dimension is positive. The theorem provides $\gamma:S\to H_Y(D)$ with $\gamma|_{\partial S}=\alpha$ and $R\gamma=\beta$ exactly. Since $R$ is over $S$ and $\beta$ is a section, $\gamma$ is a section as well. Only the initial fiber cone was used; the theorem imposes no preservation of its colimit under transport.

source.place: Relative initiality through cartesian fibrations and exact boundary lifting, Proposition 7.1.5.19(2) and Corollary 7.1.5.17. Agent expansion using the cited statements; online source, archival copy wanted.

proof.text: Uncurry the section $\gamma$ as follows. For an $m$-simplex $y:\Delta^m\to Y$, set $\sigma=\pi y$, write $\gamma(\sigma)=(\sigma,h_\sigma)$, and set $\widetilde a(y)=h_\sigma(\operatorname{id}_{\Delta^m},y)$ on the diagonal simplex of $\Delta^m\times_S Y$. Restriction identities $h_{\sigma\theta}=h_\sigma\circ(\theta\times\mathrm{id})$ make this a simplicial map. The restriction component of $R\gamma=\beta$ gives $\widetilde a|_{i_X(X)}=a|_{i_X(X)}$, while its postcomposition component gives $p\widetilde a=b$. The equality $\gamma|_{\partial S}=\alpha$ gives $\widetilde a=a$ on $\pi^{-1}(\partial S)$. These subsets have union $M$ and agree on the intersection by the original map $a$, so $\widetilde a|_M=a$ exactly. This proves both required equations. The argument allows $X_0$ to be empty, in which case the assumed cone is simply a relative initial object; it never assumes colimits at any other vertex.

source.place: Uncurrying the lift and checking both exact triangles on the full prescribed union. Agent expansion using the cited statements; online source, archival copy wanted.
